title: Tariffs, Iran, and Rapid Impacts from AI
summary: Tariffs, war risk and AI economics.
assessment: The most consequential miss is the short Hormuz-disruption base case, contradicted by months of severe losses. The energy hedge rationale can still be useful despite that miss. Several AI business mechanisms are sensible conditional arguments, but adoption, causation and legal scope are less settled than the narrative sometimes suggests.

claims.claim: AI can handle longer software tasks.
claims.reason: METR supports improving human-time-equivalent task difficulty and success-probability distinctions. Its metric is not elapsed autonomous time or general workplace output. The article’s broad minutes-to-hours productivity inference exceeds what the benchmark alone establishes.

evidence.title: AI task-completion time horizons
evidence.finding: Metric is human-expert task duration at a specified success probability, not AI runtime. Self-contained software tasks do not represent a full professional workday; estimates near the long-task limit are uncertain.

claims.next_check: Reproduce February model-specific 50%/80% estimates and confidence intervals, separating runtime from task difficulty.
